event.title: Add the Predictable Code analysis workflow
event.author: predictable-code[bot]
event.body:
This adds one workflow. Merging it is what turns Predictable Code on for this repository.

**What it does when it runs.** Translates the code, analyses it, infers requirements, and
commits the analysis to one branch of its own, `predictable-code-database`, under the name of
the branch it analysed. It never commits to your branches — no source file is changed — and
opens no pull request for an analysis; a fix or a specification it writes for you is still
proposed as a pull request.

**Where it runs.** On your own runner, on your account, spending your Actions minutes. The
hosted Control Center dispatches it and reads the analysis from that branch; it never runs
your code and stores no copy of it.

**What it reads.** The analysis on that branch, and — when you open a finding — the one source
file that finding is about, so the app can show you the code beside the claim. Both are read
on demand through the App's installation access to this repository, and neither is written
anywhere on our side.

**What it needs from you.** No secret, and no configuration. The job authenticates to the
control plane with the OIDC token GitHub mints for it, and receives a short-lived download
of the CLI in return — so there is nothing to provision and nothing to rotate.

**How to turn it off.** Delete this file. That is the whole of it — no console, no setting
of ours, nothing left behind.

It runs only on `workflow_dispatch`, so merging it starts nothing by itself.
